examples.name: Basic action menu from a button
examples.description: The common case - a button trigger opening a searchable action list.

examples.name: Icon-button row menu, no search
examples.description: A dense row-level '...' menu - showSearch is false since a 3-4 item list doesn't need filtering.

examples.name: Right-aligned menu from a trailing trigger
examples.description: alignment='right' keeps the panel from overflowing past the trigger's right edge when the trigger sits near the end of a row.
examples.jsx:
<DropdownMenu
  aria-label="Table row actions"
  open={open}
  onOpenChange={setOpen}
  alignment="right"
  showSearch={false}
  sections={[{ id: 'actions', items: rowActionItems }]}
>
  <IconButton aria-label="Row actions" onClick={() => setOpen((current) => !current)}>
    <MoreVertIcon size="sm" decorative />
  </IconButton>
</DropdownMenu>

antiExamples.name: Passing a content prop the way Popup allows
antiExamples.reason: DropdownMenu has no content prop - it always renders a Menu built from sections. For arbitrary non-Menu floating content, compose Popup directly instead of forcing it through DropdownMenu.

antiExamples.name: Expecting a selection to close the dropdown automatically
antiExamples.jsx:
<DropdownMenu open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen} sections={[{ id: 'a', items: [{ id: 'delete', label: 'Delete', onSelect: handleDelete }] }]}>
  <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Actions</Button>
</DropdownMenu>
antiExamples.reason: Neither Menu nor DropdownMenu calls onOpenChange on selection. Clicking 'Delete' here runs handleDelete but leaves the dropdown open - call setOpen(false) from inside onSelect instead.
